 PFC Q2 Net Profit Dips Marginally to Rs 7,681 Cr
 By Rediff Money Desk , New Delhi 
 1 Minute Read Listen to Article 
 Share:     
 Nov 04, 2026 14:57
 x 
 PFC reports a marginal 2% dip in Q2 net profit to Rs 7,681.51 crore due to higher expenses. Total income rose slightly, and the company declared an interim dividend. Illustration: Dominic Xavier/Rediff Key Points
 PFC's consolidated net profit marginally dipped by 2% to Rs 7,681.51 crore in Q2 FY27.
 The slight dip in profit was primarily attributed to higher expenses, which rose over 3%.
 Total income for the quarter increased by 1.15% to Rs 29,234.42 crore.
 PFC's consolidated loan asset book stood at Rs 11,89,152 crore as of September 30.
 The company declared an interim dividend of Rs 4.10 per share.
 New Delhi, Nov 4 (PTI) State-owned PFC on Wednesday posted a marginal dip of around 2 per cent in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,681.51 crore in the September quarter of FY27, citing higher expenses. 
 It had clocked a profit of Rs 7,834.39 crore "from continuing and discontinued operations" in the second quarter of the preceding 2025-26 financial year, the company said in a statement.
 During the latest July-September period, the company's total income stood at Rs 29,234.42 crore, just 1.15 per cent up from Rs 28,901.10 crore in the same period a year ago.  
 The company increased its expenses to Rs 19,453.12 crore from Rs 18,843.74 crore, posting a year-on-year (y-o-y) rise of over 3 per cent.  
 In a separate statement, the company said its consolidated loan asset book stood at Rs 11,89,152 crore as on September 30.  
 Until September this year, PFC has raised around USD 1.4 billion under the concessional foreign exchange swap facility introduced by the RBI for pubic sector enterprises, which is available until December 31, 2026.  
 During the reporting quarter, the company also declared an interim dividend of Rs 4.10 per share.  
 Under the Ministry of Power, Power Finance Corporation (PFC) is a leading non-banking financial corporation in the country focussing on energy projects. -->
